question: Shoppers judged four identical pairs of stockings laid out in a row. Which pair did they most often pick as best?
options: The pair on the far right
The pair on the far left
answer: The pair on the far right, chosen almost four times as often as the far left. Asked why, shoppers cited knit, sheerness or elasticity; nobody mentioned position, and almost all denied it could matter when asked. People report plausible reasons, not the real ones. The shelf decided; the shopper wrote the explanation.
move: Being able to give a reason does not mean it was the reason.
ask: For a recent choice I explained confidently, could something I never noticed have decided it?
trap: No pair: with identical stockings, nothing else should sway the choice.
reference: Nisbett & Wilson, Telling more than we can know: Verbal reports on mental processes, Psychological Review, 1977
